evidence.excerpt: Alternating layers of poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDADMAC) and poly(sodium 4-styrenesulfonate) (PSS) were deposited on corona-treated LLDPE substrates via dip-coating at pH 4.0 and ionic strength 0.1 M NaCl. Films with 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20 bilayers were produced and OTR measured at 23 °C and 50 % RH. OTR decreased from 1720 cm³/(m²·day·bar) for uncoated LLDPE to 210 cm³/(m²·day·bar) at 20 bilayers; total coating thickness was 380 nm by profilometry. Adhesion of the coating was assessed by tape-peel and cross-cut tests; failure occurred at the coating–substrate interface for samples with fewer than 8 bilayers, suggesting inadequate corona treatment recovery. Humid ageing at 85 % RH for 14 days caused an OTR increase of 35 % at 20 bilayers. The coating approach is positioned as an EVOH-free route to moderate oxygen barrier on flexible polyolefin substrates.
